points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 德彪西于1862年8月22日出生在巴黎郊外的圣日耳曼昂莱，是家中五个孩子中的长子。他的父亲是一家瓷器店的店主，母亲是裁缝。尽管家庭并不富裕，但德彪西从小就展现出非凡的音乐天赋。7岁时，他开始学习钢琴，并在当地一位钢琴教师塞西尔·肖米安的指导下接受早期音乐教育。这段时期，德彪西对音乐有着独特的感受力，对传统音乐教育中的规则表现出不耐烦，这预示了他后来音乐革新的方向。
points.descriptionEn: Claude Debussy was born on August 22, 1862, in Saint-Germain-en-Laye, a suburb of Paris, as the eldest of five children in a modest family. His father owned a china shop and his mother was a seamstress. Despite limited financial means, Debussy displayed extraordinary musical talent from a young age. At age 7, he began piano studies under local teacher Cécille Chaminade, receiving his early musical education. During this period, Debussy showed a unique sensitivity to music and demonstrated impatience with the rules of traditional musical instruction, foreshadowing his later musical innovations.

points.title: 巴黎音乐学院岁月
points.description: 1872年，10岁的德彪西进入巴黎音乐学院，开始了长达12年的专业音乐学习。在这里，他接受了系统的古典音乐训练，但与学院派的传统格格不入。德彪西对当时的音乐教学方式感到不满，尤其对巴赫、贝多芬等古典大师的权威性持怀疑态度。然而，这段时期他接触到了俄罗斯音乐，特别是穆索尔斯基的作品，这对他后来的音乐风格产生了深远影响。1884年，德彪西凭借《浪子》获得罗马大奖，得以前往罗马梅第奇别墅进修，这是他音乐生涯的重要转折点。
points.descriptionEn: In 1872, at age 10, Debussy entered the Paris Conservatory, beginning 12 years of professional musical training. Here, he received systematic classical music education but felt out of place with the conservatory's traditional approach. Debussy was dissatisfied with the teaching methods of the time and particularly skeptical of the authority of classical masters like Bach and Beethoven. However, during this period, he was exposed to Russian music, especially the works of Mussorgsky, which profoundly influenced his later musical style. In 1884, Debussy won the Prix de Rome with his cantata 'L'enfant prodigue,' earning him a scholarship to study at the Villa Medici in Rome, marking a significant turning point in his musical career.

points.title: 罗马留学时期
points.description: 1885年至1887年，德彪西在罗马梅第奇别墅度过。这段时期本应是他学习古典传统的黄金时光，但德彪西却对学院派的严格要求感到窒息。他很少按照要求完成规定的作品，反而沉浸在罗马的艺术氛围中，研究文艺复兴时期的绘画和雕塑。德彪西对意大利传统音乐也持批判态度，认为其过于刻板。这段经历强化了他对传统音乐规则的叛逆精神，同时也促使他开始探索新的音乐表达方式。1887年，德彪西提前结束罗马学业返回巴黎，标志着他与学院派正式决裂。
points.descriptionEn: From 1885 to 1887, Debussy studied at the Villa Medici in Rome. This period was intended to be his golden time for learning classical traditions, but Debussy found the academic requirements stifling. He rarely completed the required compositions as instructed, instead immersing himself in Rome's artistic atmosphere, studying Renaissance paintings and sculptures. Debussy was also critical of Italian musical traditions, finding them too rigid. This experience reinforced his rebellious spirit against musical conventions and prompted him to explore new forms of musical expression. In 1887, Debussy left Rome prematurely, marking his formal break with academic traditions.

points.title: 印象派音乐大师
points.description: 1890年代至1910年代初，德彪西在巴黎创作了他最具代表性的作品，确立了印象派音乐的地位。1894年，他的《牧神午后前奏曲》首演，这部作品被视为印象派音乐的里程碑，打破了传统和声与结构的束缚。1901年，德彪西开始创作《大海》，这部管弦乐作品展现了他对自然声音的独特捕捉能力。1902年，歌剧《佩利亚斯与梅丽桑德》首演，进一步巩固了他的艺术地位。这一时期，德彪西与象征主义诗人马拉美等艺术家交往密切，他们的艺术理念相互影响。德彪西的音乐强调色彩、氛围和情感暗示，而非传统叙事，这种创新使他成为现代音乐的先驱。
points.descriptionEn: From the 1890s to the early 1910s, Debussy lived in Paris and created his most representative works, establishing impressionist music. In 1894, his 'Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune' premiered, considered a milestone of impressionist music that broke free from traditional harmony and structure. In 1901, Debussy began composing 'La mer,' an orchestral work showcasing his unique ability to capture natural sounds. In 1902, his opera 'Pelléas et Mélisande' premiered, further solidifying his artistic status. During this period, Debussy associated closely with symbolist poets like Mallarmé, with their artistic ideas mutually influencing each other. Debussy's music emphasized color, atmosphere, and emotional suggestion rather than traditional narrative, making him a pioneer of modern music.

points.title: 晚期创作与影响
points.description: 1910年至1918年，德彪西进入创作晚期，尽管受到第一次世界大战的影响和健康问题（癌症）的困扰，他仍创作了一系列重要作品。1913年，他的《钢琴练习曲》出版，展现了作曲家对钢琴技巧的全新探索。1915年，德彪西完成了《小提琴奏鸣曲》，这是他最后的重要作品之一。这一时期，德彪西的音乐风格更加内省和抽象，对后来的作曲家如斯特拉文斯基、拉威尔等产生了深远影响。1918年3月25日，德彪西在德国炮击巴黎期间去世，终年55岁。他的去世标志着一个音乐时代的结束，但他的音乐理念继续影响了20世纪音乐的发展。
points.descriptionEn: From 1910 to 1918, Debussy entered his late creative period. Despite being affected by World War I and health issues (cancer), he produced several important works. In 1913, his 'Études for Piano' were published, showcasing the composer's new explorations in piano technique. In 1915, Debussy completed his 'Violin Sonata,' one of his last significant works. During this period, Debussy's musical style became more introspective and abstract, profoundly influencing later composers such as Stravinsky and Ravel. On March 25, 1918, Debussy died during German shelling of Paris at age 55. His death marked the end of a musical era, but his musical ideas continued to influence the development of 20th-century music.

supporter.zh: 德彪西被视为现代音乐的先驱和革命者，他打破了传统和声与结构的束缚，创造了独特的印象派音乐风格。他的音乐强调色彩、氛围和情感暗示，而非传统叙事，为20世纪音乐开辟了新道路。德彪西的作品如《牧神午后前奏曲》、《大海》和《佩利亚斯与梅丽桑德》等，至今仍被广泛演奏和欣赏，他对后世作曲家如斯特拉文斯基、拉威尔等产生了深远影响。德彪西的艺术遗产在于他证明了音乐可以像绘画一样捕捉瞬间印象和情感，拓展了音乐表达的边界。
supporter.en: Debussy is regarded as a pioneer and revolutionary of modern music who broke free from traditional harmony and structure to create a unique impressionist musical style. His music emphasized color, atmosphere, and emotional suggestion rather than traditional narrative, paving the way for 20th-century music. Works such as 'Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune,' 'La mer,' and 'Pelléas et Mélisande' continue to be widely performed and appreciated, profoundly influencing later composers like Stravinsky and Ravel. Debussy's artistic legacy lies in demonstrating that music could capture fleeting impressions and emotions like painting, expanding the boundaries of musical expression.

critic.zh: 批评者认为德彪西的音乐缺乏深度和结构，过于依赖感官效果而缺乏思想内涵。他们指责德彪西对传统音乐的全盘否定导致音乐技巧的退步，认为他的作品虽然优美但缺乏真正的创新。一些评论家还批评德彪西的个人生活，包括他的不忠和反复无常的性格，认为这些特质反映在他的音乐中，导致作品缺乏一致性。此外，有批评者指出德彪西的印象派音乐虽然在当时具有革命性，但实际上是对浪漫主义音乐的延续而非真正的突破，只是改变了表现方式而非本质。
critic.en: Critics argue that Debussy's music lacks depth and structure, relying too heavily on sensory effects without substantial intellectual content. They accuse Debussy of wholesale rejection of musical tradition leading to a decline in technical skill, suggesting his works are beautiful but lack true innovation. Some critics also point to Debussy's personal life, including infidelities and erratic temperament, arguing these traits are reflected in his music, resulting in inconsistency. Additionally, some critics maintain that while Debussy's impressionist music was revolutionary at the time, it was actually a continuation of Romantic music rather than a true breakthrough, merely changing the mode of expression rather than the essence.

objective.zh: 从历史与流行文化视角看，德彪西被定义为连接浪漫主义与20世纪现代音乐的关键桥梁。他的音乐虽然被称为'印象派'，但实际上是对传统音乐规则的重新诠释而非完全抛弃。德彪西的作品在当代流行文化中广泛存在，从电影配乐到广告音乐都能听到他的影响。在音乐学界，德彪西被视为象征主义艺术运动在音乐领域的代表，他的创作理念与当时的视觉艺术、文学相互呼应。德彪西的遗产不仅在于他的音乐作品，还在于他改变了人们对音乐本质的理解，使音乐从纯粹的技巧展示转向更注重情感和氛围的表达。
objective.en: From a historical and popular culture perspective, Debussy is defined as a crucial bridge connecting Romanticism to 20th-century modern music. Although his music is termed 'impressionist,' it was actually a reinterpretation rather than complete rejection of musical traditions. Debussy's works remain prevalent in contemporary popular culture, with his influence heard in film scores and advertising music. In musicology, Debussy is regarded as the musical representative of the Symbolist art movement, with his creative ideas echoing contemporary visual arts and literature. Debussy's legacy lies not only in his musical compositions but in his transformation of how music is understood, shifting it from mere technical display to greater emphasis on emotional and atmospheric expression.

self.zh: 音乐始于寂静的沉默之中。
self.en: Music begins where the speech ends.

others.zh: 德彪西的音乐就像月光下的花园，神秘而美丽，每一刻都在变化，却又保持着永恒的魅力。
others.en: Debussy's music is like a garden in moonlight, mysterious and beautiful, changing with every moment yet retaining eternal charm.
